model.auto.settings.body: A bot set to Auto picks its model on every turn. For its own turns (talking with you, planning, coordinating) it uses the strongest general model you can pay for, on the engine it already runs on when it can. Whenever it hands work out (a delegated task, a routine, a goal step, a parallel task), it reads the work, its attachments and the teammate's role, sorts it (coding, long reading, quick task, deep reasoning, vision, automation, large context) and gives it the matching model: cheap tasks go to cheap models. It only uses engines your subscription, your own key or the organization's key can pay for, keeps the bot's approval level and tools, and never touches a bot pinned to a model. If an engine refuses, Auto tries the next model once, then shows the engine's own error.

triggers.setup.github: In the repository or organization: Settings > Webhooks > Add webhook. Payload URL: the URL above. Content type: application/json. Secret: the signing secret. Pick the events (Pull requests, Pull request reviews, Pull request review comments, Pull request review threads, Issue comments, Workflow runs, Issues, Pushes, Releases).
triggers.setup.gitlab: In the project: Settings > Webhooks > Add new webhook. URL: the URL above. Secret token: the signing secret. Check Merge request, Pipeline, Issues or Push events.
triggers.setup.slack: In your Slack app (api.slack.com/apps): Event Subscriptions > Enable Events, Request URL: the URL above. Subscribe to app_mention, reaction_added or message.channels. Then paste Basic Information > Signing Secret here.
triggers.setup.teams: Create a Microsoft Graph subscription (POST /subscriptions) on the channel or chat messages, with notificationUrl: the URL above and clientState: the signing secret. Graph checks the URL right away and Sagax answers. Renew the subscription before it expires.
triggers.setup.email: Create a Microsoft Graph subscription on me/mailFolders('Inbox')/messages, changeType created, notificationUrl: the URL above, clientState: the signing secret. Sender and subject filters are checked by the bot, which reads the message through its Outlook connector.
triggers.setup.calendar: Create a Microsoft Graph subscription on me/events (changeType created, updated, deleted), notificationUrl: the URL above, clientState: the signing secret. Event start comes from a connector poller, not from Graph.
triggers.setup.sentry: In Sentry: Settings > Developer Settings > Custom Integration (internal). Webhook URL: the URL above; check Issue, Error or the alert rule action. Then paste its Client Secret here.
triggers.setup.pagerduty: In PagerDuty: Integrations > Generic Webhooks (v3) > New Webhook. Webhook URL: the URL above; pick the incident events. Copy the signing secret it shows once and paste it here.
triggers.setup.linear: In Linear: Settings > API > Webhooks > New webhook. URL: the URL above; pick Issues, Comments or Cycles. Paste its signing secret here.

Viewers bind only to loopback, and exact bot-derived targets prevent one bot from attaching to another bot's container. Each VM keeps the existing 4 GB, 2 CPU, 512-process and dropped-capability limits. VMs can still reach the internet.
vm.safety.shared: Cua Driver operates only the VM's desktop. Exactly one private host folder is mounted at {path}; files and browser sign-ins there survive VM replacement, while everything elsewhere in the VM remains disposable. The password-protected viewer is available only on this machine. Docker and Podman runs are limited to 4 GB memory, 2 CPUs and 512 processes; all Linux capabilities are dropped except the two the desktop supervisor needs to switch to its unprivileged user. The VM can still reach the internet, and bots share it one at a time.
